title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
statement: Given the heights of adjacent bars (each of width 1) in a histogram, return the area of the largest rectangle that fits entirely inside the bars.

hints.1_question: For each bar, think about the widest rectangle in which that bar is the shortest one. What decides its left and right edges?
hints.2_nudge: A stack of increasing heights lets you find, for each bar, the first shorter bar on its left and on its right.
hints.3_big_hint: Scan with a sentinel 0 at the end. While the stack top is taller than h: pop it; width = i if stack is empty else i - stack[-1] - 1; area = height * width.

known_bugs.name: never flushes the stack at the end (no sentinel)
known_bugs.followup: For [2, 4] nothing is ever popped in your loop. Which bars are still on the stack when the scan ends, and who handles them?

known_bugs.name: width off by one when the stack is non-empty
known_bugs.followup: After popping a bar, the new stack top is the first shorter bar to the left. How many bars lie strictly between it and i?

known_bugs.name: expands around every bar (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: For a steadily rising histogram, how far does each bar's right expansion walk? Can a stack remember that for you?

followups: Why does a trailing sentinel of 0 remove the need for a cleanup loop?
How does this help solve Maximal Rectangle (85)?
